Dear [Hotel Partnerships Manager],

I’m Aisha Khan from Serve & See Tours. We specialise in travel for volleyball teams and are seeking a regional hotel partner to block rooms and provide on‑site services for three tournament weekends in 2026. We are proposing a negotiated rate of £95 per room per night for an anticipated 120 room nights per weekend, totalling 360 room nights across the season, plus complimentary meeting space for pre‑match briefings and a fixed team F&B package for arrival dinners.

Deliverables to your property include preferred supplier listing on our website and booking communications, co‑branded welcome signage in the hotel lobby during event weekends, two social posts per tournament tagging the hotel and an invitation to include promotional material in arrival packs. We will guarantee a minimum occupancy commitment per weekend and provide advance manifests 14 days before arrival so your team can plan staffing and provisioning.

In return the hotel benefits from predictable occupancy, ancillary revenue from F&B and meeting spaces, and targeted exposure to a demographic that frequently returns to the same operator for future travel. We will provide a short performance report after each weekend covering occupancy, guest satisfaction feedback and on‑site spend estimates.

Could you confirm if the proposed rate and meeting space availability are feasible? If agreeable, I’d like to arrange a site inspection and receive your standard master accommodation contract so we can move to a block room agreement by mid‑March.

Looking forward to your thoughts.

Warm regards,
Aisha Khan
Founder, Serve & See Tours

Emergency procedure – lost passport in Barcelona on 20 May

If a passport is lost then isolate the traveller and assign a staff member to stay with them. Confirm the loss location and time, and check immediate areas for the document.

Call the local police and obtain a lost-property or theft report. Record the police report number and officer name. Photograph the report for our records.

Contact the British Consulate in Barcelona immediately and book an appointment for an emergency travel document. Use the consulate emergency number if outside opening hours. Keep the traveller calm and gather all supporting ID copies and flight details.

Notify our insurance and start a claim for emergency costs and any rebooking fees. If the traveller needs to travel before a full passport replacement then assist with emergency travel documentation and inform the airline of the situation.

Inform the group discreetly and adjust the itinerary if necessary. If an overnight stay is required then authorise reasonable accommodation and keep receipts. If flights need rebooking then prioritise the affected traveller and reconcile costs with insurance afterwards.

FYI: Keep me updated at every stage and send copies of the police report and consulate documents to our claims inbox. We'll support the traveller through the full process.

Kind regards,
Aisha Khan

She had booked her ticket to Brussels for the big match, but as she pondered her travel options, she found herself torn. Should she take the plane or the train?

As she stood at the Gare du Nord in Paris, Emma gazed out at the sleek trains chugging in and out of the station. She had always been drawn to the romance of train travel, but was it the most efficient way to reach Brussels?
